article.title: How to Change Your HVAC Air Filter
article.summary: Change your furnace or AC filter the right way: find the slot, match the size, point the airflow arrow correctly, and know how often to swap it.
article.body:
A clogged filter makes your furnace and AC work harder, raises energy bills, and lets more dust circulate. Swapping it is a five-minute job. The two things people get wrong are the size and the direction.

Affiliate disclosure: some links in this guide are affiliate links. If you buy through them, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. We only recommend products we'd use ourselves.

Safety: turn the system off at the thermostat before pulling the filter, so the blower doesn't pull dust into the system while the slot is open.

Steps

  1. Turn off the system

    Set the thermostat to off. Wait a minute for the blower to stop.

    Done right: no air is moving through the vents.

  2. Find the filter

    Most filters sit in a slot where the return duct meets the furnace or air handler, or behind a large return-air grille in a wall or ceiling. Some homes have more than one return grille, each with its own filter.

    Done right: you've found every filter location in the house.

  3. Read the size and remove the old filter

    The dimensions are printed on the filter's frame (for example 16×25×1). Note them, along with the direction the airflow arrow points, then slide the old filter out. Buy a replacement filter in exactly that size.

    Done right: you have the exact size written down, including the thickness.

  4. Insert the new filter with the arrow toward the furnace

    The arrow on the frame shows the direction air flows. Point it toward the furnace or blower, away from the return duct you're facing.

    Done right: the arrow points toward the equipment, and the filter sits flat in its slot with no gaps around the edges.

  5. Write the date and restart

    Write today's date on the new filter's frame, close the slot or grille, and turn the system back on. Set a reminder for the next change.

    Done right: air is flowing at the vents, and the date is visible on the filter.

Call an HVAC technician if: the filter turns black quickly, you see dust blowing from vents even with a new filter, there's no filter slot at all, or the system makes new noises after a change.

FAQ

How often should I change my air filter?

For standard 1 in filters, every 1–3 months. Change it monthly if you have pets, allergies or construction dust. Thicker 4–5 in media filters often last 6–12 months.

Which way does the arrow go on an air filter?

Toward the furnace or air handler, in the direction the air is moving.

What MERV rating should I buy?

Many homes do well with MERV 8–11. Higher ratings trap more particles but can restrict airflow in some systems, so check your equipment manual.

Can I use a filter that's slightly smaller?

No. Air bypasses a filter that doesn't fill the slot, and the dust goes straight into the system.
